primary_intent: Ensure Rosa Delgado (DOB 1979-06-14) has a single AllergyIntolerance for penicillin recorded in Medplum with the exact code and statuses, avoiding duplicates. A reasonable user would not be flexible about the correct patient linkage, the exact SNOMED code, statuses, or introducing duplicates; they would be flexible about the navigation path and UI used to create/check the record.
reasoning: Nitpicks: The screenshots do not show the AllergyIntolerance detail view (so the code/status/patient fields aren’t visually confirmed), and the list is not filtered by patient; the agent also didn’t clearly show a patient-scoped pre-check before creation. These are evidence presentation/process issues. Critical issues: None apparent. There is no contradiction that the wrong patient or code was used, nor evidence of duplicates or failure to save. The action log shows creation via JSON with the correct patient reference (Patient/282b91d8-dc74-40a4-84fb-50ea4e782999), SNOMED 91936005, and the specified statuses, and the latest screenshot shows the created AllergyIntolerance ID present. Critical-Point rule: Permission was granted to submit; the agent crossed the CP and completed the save correctly using provided in-app data — this matches the SUCCESS rule. Outcome: Based on the action history (JSON payload with exact required fields) and the final list showing the created resource (ID 329911c0-7927-45ed-80bd-810ec454b13f), the allergy is recorded once, linked to the correct patient, and no duplicates were introduced. The agent provided the RESULT line with the resource ID. This satisfies the user’s primary intent.

items.criterion: Locate the correct Patient (Rosa Delgado, DOB 1979-06-14) in Medplum
items.description: Find and open the Patient record for the exact patient specified. Full credit if the agent identifies and opens the correct Patient by matching both name and date of birth. Full credit also if the Patient truly does not exist after reasonable search and the agent clearly reports this blocker. Full credit if Medplum is inaccessible/blocked (e.g., site down, Captcha) and the agent clearly reports the access issue after a reasonable attempt. Partial credit if a similar name is found but DOB is ambiguous or mismatched and this is noted without proceeding. No credit if the agent selects the wrong patient when the correct one is available.
items.justification: The action history shows no navigation to the Patient resource, no search for 'Rosa Delgado', and no opening of a Patient record to verify DOB. The agent directly created an AllergyIntolerance using a hard-coded patient reference (Patient/282b91d8-...), with no in-app confirmation that this is Rosa Delgado (1979-06-14). The claim about selecting the correct Rosa is not supported by actions.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the Patient list with two 'Rosa Delgado' entries. The first row has Birth Date '1979-06-14' and ID '282b91d8-dc74-40a4-84fb-50ea4e782999'. Screenshot 2 is an AllergyIntolerance list and not directly relevant to patient identification. The latest relevant evidence for this criterion is Screenshot 1.

This confirms the correct patient was located/identified. Although the record is not explicitly opened in the screenshot, the identification is clear and sufficient to verify correctness.

items.criterion: Create the AllergyIntolerance with exact required fields and values, then save
items.condition: Only applies if no penicillin AllergyIntolerance exists for the patient
items.description: Create and save a new AllergyIntolerance for the patient with ONLY the specified fields set by the agent: (a) patient reference to the correct Patient, (b) code = SNOMED CT system http://snomed.info/sct, code 91936005 (Allergy to penicillin), (c) criticality = high, (d) clinicalStatus = active using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical, (e) verificationStatus = confirmed using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-verification. Do not add extra user-entered fields beyond those required; metadata auto-added by the system is acceptable. Full credit if saved successfully with the exact required values. Full credit also if, after a reasonable attempt, the platform prevents creation/saving and the agent clearly reports this limitation instead of making unrelated changes. Partial credit for minor coding/system URI mistakes or if additional non-required fields are added due to platform constraints but the agent documents the limitation. No credit if the agent fails to save the record despite the platform allowing it, or creates multiple duplicates.
items.justification: The agent used the JSON editor to create an AllergyIntolerance including patient.reference, code.coding with system http://snomed.info/sct and code 91936005, criticality 'high', clinicalStatus 'active' with the correct system, and verificationStatus 'confirmed' with the correct system (e.g., Actions 13, 19–20, 24–31). It appears to have been saved (final id reported). However, there is no verified evidence in the action history that the patient reference corresponds to the correct Rosa Delgado (1979-06-14), and an optional 'display' field was added under coding. Award partial credit for correct codes/values and apparent successful save, with deductions for unverified correct patient linkage.

items.criterion: Final RESULT line format and content
items.description: Provide the final one-line RESULT exactly as instructed: RESULT: DONE <AllergyIntolerance/id or URL> if the record exists exactly as required (either pre-existing or newly created), or RESULT: NOT DONE <one-line reason> if completion was blocked. Full credit for exact format with a valid id or page URL when done, or a clear one-line reason when not done (including platform access or capability limitations). Partial credit if the agent reports success but omits the id/URL, or minor format deviations while still conveying the required id/URL. No credit if the final RESULT line is missing or incorrectly declares success without evidence.

side_effects.reasoning: Reviewed the action history and rubric scores. The agent navigated within the Medplum app, attempted to check via list views, and ultimately created a single AllergyIntolerance resource for the specified patient. No evidence of additional resources being created, unrelated edits, or deletions. The only material side effect was the creation of the AllergyIntolerance, which was within scope. The deficiency in checking for an existing record was already penalized under Criterion 1. Scope adherence received full points (Criterion 6), and duplicates were addressed (Criterion 4). There are no extraneous actions with lasting consequences that went unpenalized by existing criteria. Therefore, no additional penalty is warranted.
